title: An AI Says It Solved Kakeya, in Every Dimension
importance_reason: public: Lino's YouTube channel, in a narrator voice, explaining a harmonic-analysis result nobody independent has checked yet; a viewer may repeat any claim
audience: A curious viewer on YouTube: a smart high-schooler, or someone from another field, who saw the headline that OpenAI's AI proved the Kakeya conjecture and knows no harmonic analysis. After watching, they can say what the needle problem and the Kakeya conjecture are, what local smoothing says about waves, why waves imply needles, the core idea of the new proof in plain words, what it changes and does not, and how far to trust it today.

youtube.title: OpenAI Says Its AI Solved the Kakeya Conjecture in Every Dimension (Opus 5.5 Explains)
alternatives: How Little Room Does a Needle Need? OpenAI Says Its AI Finished Kakeya (Opus 5.5 Explains)
Zero Area, Full Size: the Kakeya Conjecture and OpenAI's Claimed Proof, Explained
description: On October 26, OpenAI posted a paper saying its AI had proved the local smoothing conjecture for the wave equation in every dimension, and with it the Kakeya conjecture. Kakeya started in 1917 with a question: how little room do you need to turn a needle around? The answer turned out to be almost none, and the question grew into a conjecture about how big a set with a needle pointing in every direction has to be.

I had Opus 5.5 explain it from the ground up, for anyone who knows no harmonic analysis: the needle puzzle, why a set with a needle in every direction can have zero area, how size is measured by painting a shape with smaller and smaller brushes, why waves lead back to needles, the idea behind the new proof, and how far to trust it. As far as I could find, as of October 30, 2026, no independent check had been reported.

I made this video with ShipShow, my open-source toolkit of skills and plugins that lets AI agents build narrated videos like this one, end to end. The narrator is an invented voice, not a real person. https://github.com/latent-variable/shipshow
